study_only_governance.why_now: The ring-buffer packet already lands its boundary checklist plus overwrite, wakeup, mapping, ioctl, reader-page, read-page, and tracefs reader-serialization audits, and it now carries an explicit maintenance-mode handoff so the next honest posture is parked study-only governance rather than another invented review-only follow-up.

decision_checklist.summary: Keep reserve and commit publication in C while the survey records the lockless boundary around nested writers.
decision_checklist.rationale: The reserve and commit path still couples cmpxchg transitions to nested writer ordering and per-CPU commit movement, so Phase 14 should record the decision boundary rather than claim wrapper ownership.

decision_checklist.summary: Treat head-page rotation and reader-page extraction as a stay-in-C handoff boundary.
decision_checklist.rationale: The reader-page swap spans head-page movement, commit-page adjacency, and page handoff semantics that are documented upstream but still too coupled for a wrapper-first move.

decision_checklist.summary: Keep remote-reader metadata and reader-page import decisions in C while the survey records their callback boundary.
decision_checklist.rationale: Remote readers add callback-driven metadata refresh and reader-page import rules on top of the local ring-buffer model, so the current lane should only name the boundary and not invent Zig ownership.

decision_checklist.summary: Keep wakeups, poll watermarks, and mmap reader publication in C while the survey records their tracefs-facing boundary.
decision_checklist.rationale: Wait queues, irq_work handoff, full-waiter watermark state, and mmap meta-page refresh all share the same reader-visible contract, so Phase 14 should audit those seams together instead of implying a wrapper can safely own any one piece in isolation.

decision_checklist.summary: Keep mapped-reader resize, snapshot, and splice limitations in C while the survey records their shared tracefs lockout boundary.
decision_checklist.rationale: A mapped reader pins `resize_disabled`, blocks snapshot-style buffer swaps for mapped pages, and forces tracefs splice reads onto the copying path, so the mapping limitations remain one shared C-owned contract rather than a wrapper-first seam.

decision_checklist.summary: Keep reader-page acquisition, consuming reads, and iterator start in C while the survey records their shared reader-lock and resize boundary.
decision_checklist.rationale: Reader-page acquisition can swap the out-of-ring reader page with the head page, publish lost-event deltas, and wait for writer-side commits, while both consuming reads and iterator start take reader-side locks and pin `resize_disabled`, so the current lane should record one combined handoff rather than imply a wrapper can own any one piece safely.

gaps.why_now: The existing Phase 14 build step is the smallest honest place to carry a study-only ring-buffer survey beside the already-landed workqueue boundary map without implying a new bridge implementation.
The existing make target keeps the ring-buffer survey runnable with the same bounded discipline as the other tranche gates.
The freeze map already records `kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c` as study-only, so the survey can anchor itself in an explicit stay-in-C policy instead of creating momentum toward a premature port.
A dedicated Phase 14 survey gate is the smallest truthful way to keep the ring-buffer size, supporting docs, and blocked port status reviewable without shipping a `ring_buffer.zig` surface.
A lane note keeps the roadmap gap explicit by comparing the 8k-line anchor and its consumer-facing docs against the current Phase 14 stay-in-C posture.

This lane now carries a small decision checklist around reserve or commit ownership, reader-page rotation, and remote callback boundaries so the ring-buffer survey names the first reviewable seams before any bridge candidate is entertained.

The lane now records one small overwrite and lost-event audit around `rb_move_tail()`, overwrite mode, and reader-side lost-event reporting so the next review stops rediscovering where full-buffer accounting stays coupled to the C implementation.

The lane now records a narrow wakeup and mmap audit around `rb_wake_up_waiters()`, `rb_watermark_hit()`, `ring_buffer_wait()`, `ring_buffer_poll_wait()`, and meta-page refresh so tracefs wait queues, watermark state, and mapped-reader publication remain explicit stay-in-C seams.

The lane now records one small tracefs mapping limitation audit around resize prohibition, snapshot incompatibility, and splice copy fallback so mapped-reader lockouts stay explicit before any bridge candidate is entertained.

The lane now records a narrow mapped-reader ioctl audit around `TRACE_MMAP_IOCTL_GET_READER`, `ring_buffer_map_get_reader()`, lost-event publication, and concurrent mapped-reader handoff so the tracefs ioctl path stays explicit before any bridge candidate is entertained.

The lane now records a narrow reader-page consume audit around `rb_get_reader_page()`, `ring_buffer_read_start()`, and `ring_buffer_consume()` so reader-page swaps, lost-event publication, iterator setup, and consuming reads stay explicit before any bridge candidate is entertained.

The lane now records a narrow read-page extraction audit around `ring_buffer_alloc_read_page()`, `ring_buffer_read_page()`, partial-copy versus page-swap behavior, and the `resize_disabled` handoff so exported-page reads stay explicit before any bridge candidate is entertained.

The lane now records a narrow tracefs reader-serialization audit around `trace_access_lock()`, `tracing_buffers_read()`, and the read-versus-splice consumed-page lifetime rule so per-CPU readers, all-buffer readers, and page-release ownership stay explicit before any bridge candidate is entertained.

The parked packet now carries explicit replay commands, reopen conditions, and a future truthfulness-only target so later runs can keep the study-only posture disciplined without inventing a new bridge or audit seam.

The roadmap allows `kernel/trace/ring_buffer.zig` only if years of evidence justify it, and the current survey still shows deep commit, per-CPU page, reader, wakeup, mmap, and overwrite coupling that should remain in the C implementation.
